- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.80) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.20) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; increase forecast by 1–2% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.80 to -0.20 within 3 days), model fails to adjust quickly; apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment >0.50 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overreact; cap forecast growth at 2–3% per day unless sentiment >0.80.
